title: Stateful runtime upgrade orchestrator + safety-net for private VPC rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
We need an automated, auditable rollout and rollback orchestration for private (VPC) data-plane runtime upgrades that preserves in-flight state and maintains zero-downtime for customer traffic. Unlike previous stateless rollout strategies, private deployments host stateful caches and long-lived connections (KV cache shards, active session leases) that require coordinated transfer, pre-warm, and safety-net rollback steps.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Upgrade process performs canary -> staggered rollouts with progressive traffic shift and shadow verification; ability to abort and rollback within SLA window.
- No customer-visible 5xx spikes or token-level latency SLO violations during a successful upgrade (monitoring thresholds described below).
- Stateful KV cache transfer or pre-warming reduces cold-start amplification by >= 70% compared to naive restart.
- Rollback path must be deterministic, idempotent, and execute safely when partial migration occurred (e.g., 30% of nodes upgraded).
- All orchestration triggered via Terraform/Terraform modules and an operator/controller that reconciles cluster state; rollouts and runbook links are emitted in deployment logs.

Design notes & trade-offs considered:
- Option A (in-place drain + migrate): drain replicas, migrate KV ownership, restart with new binary. Pros: simpler resource footprint. Cons: risk of prolonged degraded throughput when many replicas drain simultaneously.
- Option B (shadow/dual-deploy): bring up new variant alongside old, warm caches via replicated traffic and controlled prefix replay, then cut traffic. Pros: near-zero-downtime. Cons: higher temporary resource usage and more complex routing.
- Decision: implement hybrid dual-deploy for critical clusters (high qps, sensitive customers) and in-place for low-utilization clusters. Hybrid chosen for safety vs cost.

Concrete plan / automation components:
1) Terraform module extensions
   - new module: redwood_private/runtime_rollout (published in our internal registry). Responsible for lifecycle of rollout CRs, SSM/parameter store flags, and attaching IAM roles for the rollout operator.
   - module exposes controls: desired_batch_size, canary_ratio, prewarm_replica_count, drain_grace_sec, kv_sync_timeout, metrics_thresholds.
   - integrate with existing private deployment modules (networking, autoscaling) via explicit input outputs to avoid drift.
   (Implementation note: use Terraform 1.7 local-exec only for registering rollouts; reconcile executed by operator to avoid long-running terraform apply.)

2) Rollout operator (K8s/controller or lightweight VM service depending on customer topology)
   - Reconciliation loop reads Rollout CR: phases (PREWARM -> CANARY -> SCALEUP -> SHIFT_TRAFFIC -> VALIDATE -> PROMOTE). Supports manual pause at each step.
   - PREWARM: spin up new variant replicas with read-only shadow traffic and KV prefetch using recorded request traces.
   - CANARY: route small percentage (canary_ratio) of weighted traffic. Run smoke checks (latency, error rate, output fidelity using eval harness).
   - SHIFT_TRAFFIC: progressive traffic shift in batches (desired_batch_size) with health-probes gating each step.
   - ROLLBACK: operator triggers reverse steps, drains new replicas, reassigns routing, and cleans up partially created resources.

3) Stateful data handling
   - KV cache handoff: implement a fast snapshot & delta-sync path for compact shards so new nodes can warm quickly; fallback to prefix-replay if snapshot fails.
   - In-flight sessions: support session affinity window and sticky proxies; migration strategy to rehydrate session state into new nodes.

4) Safety nets & observability
   - Define SLO guardrails: >=99.5% successful responses < 300ms at 95th percentile during rollout.
   - Automatic abort conditions: cumulative 5xx > 0.5% over 5m, P95 latency regression > 30% vs baseline, model-output divergence tests failing N-of-M.
   - Emit rollouts to audit log (CloudTrail-like), link to Grafana dashboard with rollout panel (dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/private-rollouts/rollout-overview).
   - Create structured runbook steps with remediation playbooks that operator can auto-execute.

5) Testing and validation
   - E2E harness: replay recorded production traces into a staging VPC, simulate prewarm and canary, measure cold-start and tail-latency.
   - Chaos tests: node failures during PREWARM and SCALEUP, KV snapshot corruption simulation, forced latency increases.
   - Integration tests: Terraform plan output validation and operator acceptance tests (GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345).

Progress updates (timeline):
- 2026-02-20 (Maya): Initial proposal drafted; held scoping session with PM/Design/Infra. Decided on hybrid approach; scoped Terraform API changes.
- 2026-02-27 (Luca): Prototype operator state machine implemented; PREWARM flow can boot new replica and perform prefix-replay against synthetic traffic. PR opened: runtime#2345.
- 2026-03-03 (QA): E2E harness ingested 72 hours of production trace; preliminary results show 65% cold-start reduction with snapshot+delta vs baseline.
- 2026-03-08 (Security review): Raised key-handling concerns for snapshot transfer. Decided to use ephemeral KMS-wrapped objects; ticket created in security backlog.
- 2026-03-11 (SRE): Observability panels added; initial alert thresholds for rollout abort tuned down to reduce noise.
- 2026-03-13 (Luca): Canary rollout executed against staging cluster; observed unexpected 12% P95 increase when prewarm replicas < 2 for large models. Increased prewarm_replica_count to 3 in module defaults.

Open issues / risks:
- Snapshot durability and cross-AZ transfer costs: need cost analysis before enabling dual-deploy by default for all customers.
- Terraform -> operator contract: race conditions possible if apply is re-run mid-rollout. Mitigation: add stable rollout token in state and lock via SSM parameter store.
- Rollback complexity for partial data migrations: need an idempotent reverse-delta algorithm for KV; high risk if not thoroughly tested.

Acceptance criteria for merging to main branch:
- Terraform module published and consumed in internal registry with documented inputs/outputs.
- Operator passes smoke e2e in staging and chaos tests for the three biggest private clusters.
- Runbook and automated rollback validated in a blue/green rehearsal with SRE.
- Security review closed for snapshot transfer and KMS usage.

Next steps / action items:
- Luca: land PR for rollout CRD and operator (runtime#2345) and address comments from SRE by 2026-03-17.
- Maya: finalize Terraform module naming and create examples for customers (example manifests + policy) by 2026-03-18.
- QA: extend e2e harness to include failure injection for KV delta-sync by 2026-03-20.
- SRE: run a dry-run upgrade of a low-traffic VPC next week and collect telemetry; schedule a post-mortem rehearsal.

- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345
- Staging rollout logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/l/rollout/ENG-15809/2026-03-11

Review requests / reviewers:
- @Priya Malik (SRE) for rollback correctness and alerts
- @Owen Park (Security) for KMS/snapshot flow
- @Camila Ruiz (PM) for customer impact gating and rollout policies

Notes for the on-call runbook (short):
- If rollout abort triggers automatically, operator will: 1) mark Rollout CR status=ABORTING, 2) stop traffic shift, 3) initiate ROLLBACK phase which drains new replicas and reassigns routing.
- If rollback fails to converge within kv_sync_timeout, open PagerDuty to SRE owner and fall back to emergency traffic re-route to control-plane fallback pool (docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Private+Fallback+Pool).

This ticket is scoped to implement the orchestration primitives, Terraform wiring, and proof-of-concept canary in staging. Full rollout to production will be gated behind acceptance criteria above and a final SRE sign-off.
